tagline: Down SR 374 from gorge to gorge in the Blackhand sandstone.
intro: SR 374 leaves US 33 near Rockbridge and runs south through Hocking State Forest and Hocking Hills State Park, ending east of South Bloomingville at SR 56. Streams have cut gorges and recess caves along the way into the Blackhand Sandstone, the same rock on which early settlers in Muskingum County found an ancient black handprint.

Part of the road began as an unnumbered gravel lane, taken into the state system in 1932. Many of the bigger pines were planted in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps. Prisoners from the Hocking County Honor Camp planted trees here too, with a guard going wherever they went.

moments.title: Rock House
moments.text: The one true cave among the Hocking Hills parks, with seven Gothic-arched windows and great sandstone columns holding up its massive roof.

moments.title: Conkle's Hollow
moments.text: A deep, cool gorge only 100 feet wide in places, where W. J. Conkle carved his name and the date 1797 into the west wall.

moments.title: Ash Cave
moments.text: A 700-foot horseshoe of sandstone with a waterfall dropping 90 feet off the rim, named for the mounds of ash, thought to be ancient campfires, that early settlers found beneath it.
